title: Limbic System Atlas
subtitle: Explore memory, salience, motivation and emotion across connected circuits
altText: Medial brain and circuit diagram showing hippocampus, amygdala, cingulate cortex, fornix, mammillary bodies, hypothalamus and ventral striatum.
learningObjectives: Identify major limbic structures without treating the limbic system as a single emotion centre.
Trace hippocampal, amygdala, cingulate and hypothalamic connections.
Relate circuit disruption to memory, salience, motivation, autonomic response and psychopathology.

sections.explainSimply: The limbic system is a group of connected regions that help link memory, emotion, motivation, body state and action.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Limbic functions emerge from distributed loops involving cortex, subcortex, hypothalamus and brainstem; no single “emotional brain” explains complex behaviour.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Classical Papez circuitry overlaps with broader corticolimbic networks including amygdala, hippocampal formation, cingulate cortex, orbitomedial prefrontal cortex, ventral striatum, septal area and hypothalamus. These systems integrate context, salience, reinforcement and autonomic output.
sections.thinkOfItLike: It is a meaning-and-priority network that tags experiences, links them to memory and body state, and biases what the person does next.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Trauma, epilepsy, neurodegeneration and focal lesions may alter memory, threat appraisal, motivation or autonomic regulation through different limbic circuits.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Calling the amygdala the “fear centre” or the limbic system the “emotional brain” oversimplifies distributed, context-sensitive networks.
sections.clinicalPearl: Emotion and memory are not separate modules; they continually shape one another through recurrent corticolimbic loops.
sections.practicalExample: Bilateral hippocampal injury may profoundly impair new episodic learning while leaving immediate attention and procedural learning relatively intact.
sections.limitationsCautions: Psychiatric symptoms cannot be localised to one limbic structure; interpretation requires network, developmental and contextual formulation.

anatomy.label: Hippocampal formation
anatomy.function: Supports episodic encoding, context and spatial representation
anatomy.inputs: Entorhinal cortex and multimodal association input
anatomy.connections: Amygdala, cingulate, thalamic and prefrontal systems
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Bilateral dysfunction particularly affects new declarative learning.

anatomy.label: Amygdala complex
anatomy.function: Assigns salience and coordinates learned threat and value signals
anatomy.outputs: Hypothalamic, brainstem, striatal and cortical targets
anatomy.connections: Hippocampus, vmPFC, insula and salience network
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: It modulates salience and learning rather than generating one universal emotion.

anatomy.label: Cingulate cortex
anatomy.function: Integrates motivation, conflict, pain and internal state
anatomy.inputs: Prefrontal, thalamic, limbic and interoceptive input
anatomy.outputs: Motor, autonomic and cortical control systems
anatomy.connections: Papez circuit, salience and default-mode networks
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Anterior and posterior subdivisions have distinct network roles.

anatomy.label: Fornix–mammillary pathway
anatomy.function: Carries hippocampal output through diencephalic memory circuitry
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Damage can impair recollection even when cortical memory regions remain structurally intact.

anatomy.label: Ventral striatum
anatomy.function: Integrates reward, motivation and action selection
anatomy.inputs: Prefrontal, hippocampal, amygdala and dopaminergic input
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Reward-related activation reflects learning and motivational value, not simple pleasure.

anatomy.label: Hypothalamus
anatomy.function: Coordinates endocrine, autonomic and homeostatic responses
anatomy.associatedDisorders: Stress dysregulation, sleep and appetite disturbance
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Links subjective state with bodily regulation and action readiness.
